name: IAC 2023 Delhi Winner
author: Arne Jach
notes: Low temperature, short steep and almost no agitation (just pushing the grounds down) to tame a harsh, bitter pineapple-fermentation coffee; two paper filters.
issues: Page starts the timer after the 15 s pour and flips at 1:30 of immersion; timeline here starts at the pour so the stated 2:15 total holds, with flip at ~1:40. Water given as 185 g / 185 ml. Author country not stated. Roast not stated (inferred medium: Caarabi Barbara Estate pineapple fermentation). Push-down (5 s) and flip (5 s) durations estimated.
segs: Pour 185 g at 80°C quickly, no bloom
Push grounds down 3-4 times with stirrer, don't stir
Fit 2 hot-rinsed paper filters in cap; steep
Place AeroPress on cup at 1:30 immersion
why: Built to tame a wild pineapple-fermented coffee: cool water and almost no agitation keep funky fruit pleasant instead of harsh. Made for anaerobic and co-fermented lots like many Indian specialty micro-lots.

name: WAC 2023 Champion
author: Tay Wipvasutt
grind: Coarse. 1Zpresso ZP6 at 65 clicks, or Comandante C40 at 29 clicks
notes: Unusual split dose: 16 g brewed first, with the last 2 g of coffee added at 0:45; concentrate diluted with 40 g room-temp then 40 g hot water.
issues: Page title credits Tay Wipvasutt but lists creator as 'Dag Press'. Country not stated. Bypass is mixed: +40 g room-temperature water (to 115 g) then +40 g hot water (to ~155 g, to taste); bypass_type set to 'cold water' as the closest single value. Roast not stated (inferred light: washed Kenya AB, Fieldwork Coffee). Pour (10 s), the 2 g add (10 s), and flip (5 s) durations estimated; 'add coffee' isn't an allowed action so it is a wait step.
segs: Add 16 g coffee, pour 100 g at 89°C
Circular stir 5 s with one side of a chopstick
Push plunger up to expel air, cap
Press at 1:35 for ~30 s, ~75 g yield
why: A split dose adds a late burst of fresh aromatics on top of a sweet base. Best with expressive fruity beans.

name: IAC 2022 Bengaluru
author: Shruti Vashist
grind: Fine-medium (steps say medium-fine); Baratza Encore listed as equipment, no setting given
notes: A long, slow immersion of a medium-dark coffee with a 70 g bloom pour and gentle cross stir, giving good body and a slightly acidic note.
issues: Placement not stated (regional entry). Roast stated as medium-dark (mapped to medium). Most timings not on page: only the 30 s bloom pour and 10 s wait are given; second pour (15 s), stir (10 s), flip (10 s), press (30 s) estimated and the long steep sized to fit the stated 4:30 total. Water given as 206 g / 206 mL. Filter count implied as one. Country not stated (Indian event).
segs: Wait 10 s, attach rinsed filter cap; steep
why: A long, slow immersion of a medium-dark coffee builds body with a light acidity — good for chocolaty and nutty Indian estate coffees.

name: IAC 2022 Champion
author: Pratik Sharma
notes: Two-temperature pour: a 45 g bloom at 85°C then the remaining 140 g at a cooler 81°C, with gentle cross stirring.
issues: Temperature split 85°C (45 g) then 81°C (140 g); temp_c shows 81 (main pour). Page shows a broken '°F' value (NaN). Country inferred from event name. Roast not stated (inferred light from double-washed specialty coffee). Grinder setting not given (a Timemore C2 is in the equipment list). Filter count not stated. Stir (10 s), second pour (15 s) and aerate (5 s) durations estimated.
why: Two temperatures: a hotter bloom for sweetness, a cooler main pour to keep acidity crisp. Suits Indian light roasts with fruit or citrus notes.

name: WAC 2022 Champion
author: Jibbi Little
grind: Two-step grind: first very coarse on a Timemore grinder and blow out the silverskins; then regrind at setting 4 on a Kinu Classic (roughly medium-fine). Sift out fines of about 100-200 microns if possible. Grind slightly finer for washed coffee.
notes: A double grind (coarse, remove chaff, regrind, sift fines) and a 35-stir concentrate pressed over frozen chilling balls, then topped up with 90°C water to 150 g; target TDS 1.3-1.35.
issues: Bypass amount ambiguous: page says 'bypass with 90°C water to 150g total' after ~58-64 g concentrate, so ~86-92 g (90 used here); the page's '150g total water' figure would instead imply 56 g. Optional ice: 4 frozen chilling balls (3 under, 1 on top) during the press, not counted as bypass. Roast not stated (inferred light: natural Striped Red Bourbon, Colombia). Pour (10 s) and stir (30 s) durations estimated. Perfect Coffee Water used in competition.
segs: Stir gently 35 times with small-bowled spoon
At 1:20 screw on cap, press out remaining air
Flip at 1:30 onto iced chilling balls
why: Removing chaff and fines strips out bitterness and muddiness for maximum clarity — rewards bright, clean citrus and floral coffees.

name: WAC 2021 Champion
author: Tuomas Merikanto
grind: Medium-coarse; Comandante at 27 clicks ("quite a rough guess" against Macap reference templates)
notes: Low 80°C water, coarser grind and minimal agitation to avoid harsh, tannic sourness in a light, complex coffee; brewed with Third Wave Water (espresso profile) on distilled water.
segs: Stir gently 3 times back and forth
At 1:00 push out air, attach cap; wait until 1:35
Swirl, then pour from height into second pitcher
why: Designed to avoid harsh, tannic sourness in a complex light roast: 80 °C and minimal agitation. Ideal for delicate, floral, high-acidity beans.

name: WAC 2021 Runner-up
author: Maru Mallee
grind: Medium, 23 clicks on a Comandante C40 Mk3 Nitro Blade
notes: Firm stir, then a rao-spin-style swirl and tap after flipping to flatten the bed before a gentle press; finished with a small room-temperature bypass. Water was 75% classic / 25% distilled.
issues: Water given in ml (150 ml + 36 ml), treated as grams. Brewer country not stated. Bypass is room-temperature water. Flip/swirl split within the page's 1:50-1:55 window estimated; final bypass+swirl step (10 s) estimated to reach the stated 2:30 total.
segs: Attach cap, press out air, place carafe on top; steep to 1:50
Swirl 3 times, tap down twice (rao-spin style)
Press gently until plunger touches puck
Remove brewer, shake gently to release last drops
Add 36 g room-temp water, swirl to cool
why: A firm stir and a long steep at 93 °C extract plenty of sweetness; the swirl after flipping keeps it even. A sweet, full cup from fruity or honey beans.

name: Championship Cold Water Bypass
author: Alexander Mills
notes: Short 1:00 brew of a 25 g dose, then an 80 g hot-water bypass plus 20 g room-temperature water so the cup reaches drinking temperature fast for judges.
issues: Placement not stated. Bypass is mixed: 80 g at 85°C then 20 g room-temperature water (from a shot glass); page's 250 g total = 50+100+80+20. Roast not stated; page says any natural or full-bodied washed coffee. Grinder not specified. Pour durations (10 s) estimated; flip (5 s) taken from the stated 30 s press so it ends at the 1:30 total. Country not stated.
why: Quick, strong and diluted with hot and room-temperature water — sweet, balanced and drinkable straight away. A forgiving pick for caramel and nutty mediums.

name: Citric Sweet
author: Rama Marti
notes: Slow, gentle championship recipe with a 90-second controlled gooseneck pour and an early stop to the press; Colombian Risaralda coffee.
issues: Roast not stated, set to 'any'. Bloom pour (10 s), stir (10 s) and flip (10 s) durations estimated. Final stir of the glass not included as a step.
segs: Slowly add remaining 180 g to 240 g, swirling, until 2:00
Press very gently to 4:20, stop at ~95% (don't press through)
why: A slow, gentle pour and stopping the press early keep clean citric brightness balanced by sugar sweetness — made for a washed Colombian.

name: WAC 2019 Champion
author: Wendelien van Bunnik
notes: A big 30 g dose of coarse coffee in only 100 g water, pressed at just 0:40, then diluted with 120 g hot water and cooled by pouring between pitchers to serve at ~60°C.
issues: Roast not stated (inferred light: washed El Salvador Pacas by Ozone, competition coffee). Pour (10 s), stir (15 s), flip (5 s) and press (30 s) durations estimated to fit the stated 1:15 total. Filter count not explicit (one rinsed filter implied). Bypass 120 g at 92°C added after pressing, then cooled by pouring between pitchers (untimed).
segs: Pour 100 g soft water at 92°C, start timer
Cap with rinsed paper filter, push out excess air
why: Lots of coffee and only 40 s of contact pulls sweetness fast without bitterness, then it's cooled so sweetness reads loud. Great for juicy, sweet beans.

name: WAC 2019 Runner-up
author: Benja Khemacheva
grind: Coarse, about 30 clicks on a Comandante C40 Mk3 Nitro Blade
notes: Very high 35 g dose brewed as a concentrate in 100 g water and pressed into a server pre-loaded with 100 g of 94°C water (pre-bypass).
issues: Bypass is a pre-bypass: 100 g hot water put in the server before pressing. Intro says 110 g pre-bypass but steps say 100 g (page total 210 g). Brewer country not stated. Roast not stated (inferred light: washed El Salvador Pacas, Ozone). Filter count not stated. Pour duration (10 s) estimated; cap+flip placed at 1:10-1:15 so the 30 s press ends at the stated 1:45 total.
segs: Pour 100 g water at 94°C onto 35 g coffee
Put filter cap on and flip at 1:15 onto server holding 100 g pre-bypass
Press with your elbow for 30 s
why: High dose, hot water and a pre-bypass make a round, heavy, sweet cup. Handles fruity naturals and caramel-sweet mediums well.

name: Love me some acid
author: Kata Muhel
notes: Low-temperature (81°C) championship recipe designed to highlight vibrant, acidic fruitiness, with a 15 s swirl and short 15 s press.
issues: Roast inferred as light (page says 'something vibrant, light'). Page starts the timer after the 70 g pour; pour durations (10 s each) estimated and included in the timeline. Championship placement taken from description as '2018 Portuguese AeroPress champion'.
segs: Attach rinsed filter cap at 1:00, wait to 1:20
why: Low 81 °C and a gentle swirl are designed to make acidity sing. Pick this when your bean tastes of lemon, berries or flowers.

name: WAC 2018 Champion
author: Carolina Ibarra Garay
notes: Very concentrated 34.9 g / 100 g brew, pressed into an unheated server and topped up with 60 g of 85 °C water plus 40 g of room-temperature water.
issues: Bypass is mixed: 60 g hot (85 °C) plus 40 g room-temperature water, recorded as 100 g hot water. Page total is 1:30, but 30 s sit + 30 s stir + 30 s press plus a flip runs to about 1:40. Pour (10 s) and flip (10 s) durations estimated. Roast and filter count not stated; roast inferred light (Kenyan finals coffee).
segs: Stir vigorously but carefully with chopsticks 30 s
Fit filter cap, flip onto unheated glass server
why: An extreme 35 g concentrate topped up with hot and room-temperature water — dense sweetness and body. Best with sweet naturals and honey-process beans.

name: WAC 2018 Runner-up
author: Xiaobo Zhang
grind: Quite coarse; plus 1 g ground very fine (roughly espresso-fine)
notes: Adds 1 g of espresso-fine coffee on top of a coarse 30 g bed just before flipping, then tops up with 50 g of water after pressing.
issues: Dose shown as 31 g in details but 30 g in steps (30 g coarse + 1 g fine = 31 g). Second pour (10 s) and flip (5 s) durations estimated. Bypass water temperature not stated (assumed hot). Roast and filter count not stated; roast inferred light (Kenyan finals coffee).
segs: Pour 70 g (to 170 g), then add 1 g very fine coffee
why: Low 80 °C and a coarse grind keep it bright and clean, with a sprinkle of fines for body. Suits delicate, fruity light roasts.

name: WAC 2018 Third Place
author: Evgeni Pinchukov
notes: Low-dose 15 g standard brew at 80 °C with two stirs; stop pressing when the grounds just break the surface.
issues: Pour (10 s each), stir (5 s each), and press (60 s, set to reach the stated 2:10 total) durations estimated. Roast and filter count not stated; roast inferred light (Kenyan finals coffee).
segs: Insert plunger, press until grounds just visible above water line
why: Low dose, low temperature and an early stop to the press — a light, tea-like cup for bright washed coffees.

name: WAC 2017 Champion
author: Paulina 'Panda' Miczka
notes: Two-cup concentrate (35 g Kenya Kamwangi AA, ~4.5% TDS) diluted with 160–200 g hot water; the page also gives a smaller version at 24 g per 100 ml plus ~120 ml after pressing.
issues: Bypass given as a 160–200 g range (200 used); page's 370 g total implies 220 g, which is inconsistent. Flip duration (5 s) estimated; page says press starts at 1:05 and ends at 1:35. Brewer country, roast, and filter count not stated; roast inferred light (Kenya AA competition coffee).
segs: At 0:35 attach pre-wet filter cap; wait to 1:05
why: Built on a Kenyan AA. A strong concentrate diluted afterwards keeps the vivid citrus and blackcurrant while staying sweet.

name: WAC 2017 Runner-up
author: Yusuke Narisawa
grind: Coarse with a sprinkle of fine grounds (~28 g coarse + 1.5 g very fine)
notes: Mixes two grind sizes (mostly coarse plus 1.5 g very fine) and uses a doubled paper filter for a cleaner cup, then adds 75 g hot water.
issues: Pour (10 s each), stir (15 s), and flip (10 s) durations estimated; page only gives the 1:50 end of the press. Roast stated as 'light to medium'; mapped to light. Bypass water temperature not specified. Brewer country not stated (event was in Seoul).
segs: Attach cap with 2 wet paper filters, flip
why: Two paper filters and a coarse grind make an exceptionally clean cup; the pinch of fines adds body back. Clarity-first, so delicate florals and fruit shine.

name: WAC 2016 Champion
author: Filip Kucharczyk
notes: High-dose 35 g concentrate brewed with only 150 g, then diluted with 100–120 g water to taste; designed to be easy without special tools.
issues: Bypass given as a 100–120 g range (100 used); its temperature isn't stated (assumed hot). Page total is 1:30, but the stated flip at 1:00 plus a 30 s press and flip/swirl time runs to about 1:40. Flip (5 s) and swirl (5 s) durations estimated. Brewer country (event was in Dublin), roast, and filter count not stated; roast inferred light.
why: A huge dose brewed short, then diluted: lots of sweetness and body without bitterness. Makes juicy, syrupy cups from fruity and honey-process beans.

name: WAC 2015 Champion
author: Lukas Zahradnik
grind: Grind size is a bit coarser than automatic espresso machine
notes: Vigorous 15 s stir in a 60 g bloom, with all parts preheated in 79 °C water; ratio 1:13 (page says 1:35, likely a typo). Uses a light-to-medium washed Kenyan.
issues: Total time not stated on page (computed 1:35). Second pour (10 s) and flip (10 s) durations estimated. Roast stated as 'light-to-medium'; mapped to light. Page lists ratio 1:35, which doesn't match 20 g:260 g (1:13). Name spelled both Lukas and Lucas. Filter count not stated.
segs: Pour remaining 200 g to the top
Attach rinsed filter cap, flip immediately
why: Cool water plus a hard stir, built on a washed Kenyan: bright blackcurrant and citrus with sweetness but no harshness.

name: WAC 2015 Runner-up
author: Nick Hatch
notes: Quick pour and short steep followed by a long 60 s press; page says it works even better with an Aesir filter or two paper filters.
issues: Bloom pour (10 s) and stir (5 s) durations estimated; 25 s bloom treated as counting from 0:00 so the timeline matches the stated 1:45. Bloom amount given as a 50–60 g range. Country and roast not stated; roast inferred light. Filter count not stated.
segs: Pour remaining water to 260 g within 20 s
why: Moderate temperature and a long, slow 60 s press give a balanced, sweet cup. A good all-rounder for light-medium beans with fruit and sugar notes.

name: WAC 2014 Champion
author: Shuichi Sasaki
notes: Low 78 °C water and a very slow 75 s press that stops with about 45 g of slurry left in the chamber.
issues: Page lists total time 1:40, but a 25 s bloom plus a 75 s press already fills 1:40 before the stirs and second pour, so the timeline runs to 2:00. Pour durations (5 s, 10 s) and stir durations (5 s each) estimated; bloom assumed to include the first pour. Filter count and roast not stated; roast inferred light.
segs: Press very slowly 75 s, stop with ~45 g slurry left
why: Very low 78 °C water and stopping before the dregs avoid bitterness completely, so floral and citrus notes stand out. Too gentle for chocolaty beans — they taste flat.

name: WAC 2012 Champion
author: Charlene De Buysere
grind: Coarse (grind setting listed as "All"; no grinder named)
notes: A simple no-stir recipe: short bloom, quick top-up, and a partial 30 s press.
issues: Bloom pour duration estimated (10 s). Filter count not stated. Roast not stated; inferred light (competition specialty coffee). Grind setting shown as 'All', which is unclear. Brewer country not stated on page.
segs: Pour remaining water to 250 g within 30 s
At 1:00 press 30 s, don't press all the way down
why: No stirring, a short bloom and a press that stops early keep the cup clean and sweet. A gentle method that won't strip a light, bright bean's fruit.

name: A Fruity Perspective
author: Div
grind: Medium, Hario V60 electric grinder setting 18 (EK-5 also listed)
notes: Tiny 20 g dense-slurry 'bloom' then a long 3.5-minute inverted steep, built to coax fruit notes from medium/medium-dark beans.
issues: Roast given as 'Medium or Medium-Dark'; mapped to 'medium'. Pour (10 s), slurry stir (10 s), flip (10 s) and swirl (5 s) durations estimated. Filter count not stated. Final 30 s rest happens off the brewer but included to match the page's 5:00 total.
segs: Mix into slurry, flatten bed with stirrer
Attach filter cap at 2:20, push out excess air, steep to 3:30
Rest coffee 30 s, swirl and serve
why: Coaxes fruit out of medium and medium-dark beans — a long, heavy steep that brings dark fruit out alongside chocolate.

name: AeroPress Vietnamese Iced Coffee
author: AeroPress
notes: The AeroPress company's own adaptation of the Vietnamese phin: 100% robusta pressed directly onto condensed milk, then iced. Can also be served hot.
issues: Orientation isn't stated; the Flow Control cap and pressing into the glass imply standard. Press duration isn't given (estimated 30 s). The page names robusta but no roast level; set to dark because Vietnamese robusta is traditionally dark-roasted. Ice and milk are 'to taste'.
fin: Add ice, and top with milk if you like. The condensed milk is already in the glass.
segs: Press straight into the condensed milk
kw: vietnamese viet vietnam ca phe sua da cà phê sữa đá condensed milk robusta phin sweet iced official
pre: Put 2 tablespoons of sweetened condensed milk in a glass wide enough for the AeroPress to sit on. Use 20 g robusta.
why: Built for robusta: heavy, bitter-chocolate coffee that stands up to sweet condensed milk and ice.

name: AeroTonic
author: Clem InTheCoffee
notes: A concentrated, low-temperature 1:3 shot poured over ice and tonic for a bright, fizzy coffee tonic; the page describes it as chocolatey and rich.
issues: Tonic given as 80–100 ml; bypass_g uses midpoint 90. Pour (10s) and press (30s) durations estimated; stir 10–20s taken as 15s and steep shortened to 85s so pour+stir+steep matches the stated 1:50 brew time. Ice amount listed confusingly as '80–100ml'. Simple syrup amount not given. Roast not stated.
fin: Slowly pour the pressed coffee over the ice and tonic. Optionally add lemon or lime wedges and simple syrup to taste.
segs: Pour 60 g water over 20 g coffee
kw: tonic espresso tonic coffee tonic spritz sparkling fizzy soda mixer lemon lime
pre: Fill a cup with ice and add 80–100 ml tonic water.
why: Tonic is bitter and citrusy, so bright beans pair best — lemon, berry and floral notes turn into a sparkling coffee spritz. Very roasty beans can taste medicinal with tonic.

name: Alan Adler Cold Brew
author: Alan Adler
grind: Fine (Comandante C40 Mk3 Nitro Blade grinder listed, no setting)
notes: A 2-minute 'cold brew' using room-temperature water and 60 s of continuous stirring, then diluted with ice water or ice to taste.
issues: Dilution with ice water or ice cubes 'to taste' — no amount given (bypass_g null). Pour duration estimated (10 s); headline 2:00 covers only stir + press. Water 70 g in details vs '~60-70 g' in steps. Roast not stated (Alan recommends Ethiopian Yirgacheffe), set to any. Page doesn't describe Adler; 'AeroPress inventor' from context. Filter count not stated.
fin: Dilute with ice or ice water to taste.
segs: Add room-temp water to level 1 (~60-70 g)
why: Cold water pulls sweetness and body but very little acidity. Chocolaty, nutty beans taste smooth and sweet; bright fruity ones taste flat.

name: Alan Adler Original
author: Alan Adler
notes: The inventor's original method: low 80°C water, a 10 s stir and immediate press, yielding a concentrate to dilute.
issues: Headline total 1:30 but steps total ~50 s (10 s stir + 20-40 s press); pour duration estimated (10 s), press set to 30 s. Optional hot-water top-up for an Americano with no amount, so bypass recorded as none. Roast not stated ('whatever suits your fancy'), set to any. Dose given as '1 scoop' in steps; water as fill level. Page categorizes it as 'From an Enthusiast' but calls Adler the AeroPress inventor. Header 176°F vs 175°F in step 5.
why: The inventor's original: cool 80 °C water and a fast press keep bitterness low on everyday darker roasts. Smooth and low-acid from chocolaty and nutty beans.

name: Blue Bottle
author: Blue Bottle Coffee
notes: Blue Bottle's standard inverted recipe: small 30 g bloom, top up, then a vigorous 10-stir agitation at 1:00 before pressing. Add 2–3 g coffee for a stronger cup.
issues: Roast listed as 'Light / Medium'; set to medium. Pour, stir, flip and press durations estimated; unclear whether the 30 s rest runs from the pour or after the stir (taken as after). Steps say ~200°F (93°C) vs 94°C/201°F in the header. Posted by shariar joy.
why: A vigorous stir at 1:00 and fuller extraction give a round, sweet, medium-bodied cup — the classic for balanced medium roasts.

name: Coffee Collective Brew Guide
author: Coffee Collective (Elliot Stølegaard)
notes: Short standard-orientation brew with a vacuum-sealed steep and a second front-to-back stir at 1:00. XL variant: 32 g to 460 g, plunge finishing at 1:50.
issues: Pour and first stir durations estimated. Page doesn't state a grinder setting. Country (Denmark) not stated on the page.
segs: Insert plunger, lift slightly for vacuum; wait to 1:00
Remove plunger, stir 3 times front to back
Reinsert plunger, off scale, press slowly to 1:30
why: Coffee Collective roasts light and fruity; a short sealed steep with a second stir keeps clarity while building sweetness.

name: Coffee with April
author: April Coffee
notes: Low dose (13 g) and low 88°C water for a light, juicy cup with low bitterness; designed for Kenyan or Ethiopian coffees.
issues: Roast not stated; inferred light from the Kenyan/Ethiopian coffee and 'light and juicy' description. Pour and stir durations estimated.
segs: Plunger on to stop drip; wait to 0:30
Remove plunger, pour remaining 150 g to 200 g
Press slowly, stop at hiss, by 2:00
why: A low dose and cooler 88 °C water make a light, juicy, low-bitterness cup — designed for Kenyan and Ethiopian coffees.

name: EVP's Iced Coffee
author: Peter (EVP Coffee)
notes: Medium-dark coffee (the author prefers Colombian) pressed onto ice — smooth like cold brew with a syrupy body.
issues: The author says medium-dark; set to medium on the card's three-level scale.
fin: Swirl and drink — smooth like cold brew, but with a thicker, syrupy body.
segs: Press into the iced mug, about 30 s
kw: iced smooth cold brew style syrupy colombian medium dark
pre: Put 200 g ice in the mug and set the AeroPress on top.
why: A medium-dark Colombian over ice gives a smooth, cold-brew-like but syrupy cup — chocolaty and caramel beans taste best.

name: Hoffmann AeroPress for Milk Drinks
author: James Hoffmann
grind: Fine - Medium Fine (slightly coarser than espresso but finer than drip; 'powdered sugar versus salt')
notes: A small, strong 1:5 concentrate (~65-70 g) brewed as the 'espresso' base for a milk drink, then topped with warm steamed/frothed milk.
issues: Milk amount not given (bypass_g null). Headline time 2:00 but steps only specify the 90 s steep; pour (10 s), stir (5 s), flip (10 s), swirl (5 s) and press (30 s) durations estimated, giving 2:30. Roast stated as 'darker roast' / espresso blend, mapped to dark. Water 90 g in details vs 90 ml in steps. Filter count not stated.
fin: Top with warm milk to taste.
segs: Pour 90 g just-off-boil water onto 18 g (preheated, inverted, plunger halfway)
Stir vigorously to wet all grounds and break clumps
Swirl to dislodge grounds from sides
Press slowly and gently until after the hiss (~65-70 g out)
why: A 1:5 concentrate made to carry milk. Chocolaty and nutty beans keep their flavour under milk; light fruity ones disappear or turn sour.

name: Hoffmann Iced AeroPress
author: James Hoffmann
grind: Finer end of medium, finer than pour-over
notes: Scaled-up Ultimate technique with 160 g ice in the decanter as bypass (400 g total liquid), served over more ice.
issues: Posted by user 'Sidechain W', credited to Hoffmann. Headline 4:30 covers only the 4:00 + 0:30 waits; pour (10 s), swirls (5 s each) and press (30 s) estimated. Ice listed as 160 g in steps but 160 ml in notes. Notes say to use as much hot water as possible (creator used 270 ml) vs 240 ml in steps. Filter count not stated.
segs: Pour ~240 g just-boiled water over 22 g, wetting all coffee
Insert plunger a few mm; steep 4 min
Press gently all the way onto 160 g ice
Swirl decanter to melt ice; serve over fresh ice
why: Brewed hot and flash-chilled on ice, which locks in aromatics — iced coffee that still tastes of fruit and flowers, not flat cold brew.

name: Hoffmann Ultimate (original, 99 °C)
author: James Hoffmann
notes: Low 11 g dose with no filter rinse or preheat; plunger seated immediately as a vacuum seal and a swirl instead of a stir.
issues: Headline says 3:20 but the steps add to 3:00 (steep to 2:00, rest 30 s, press 30 s); used 3:00. Pour and swirl durations estimated (10 s, 5 s). Water given as 200 g in details but 200 mL in steps. Filter count not stated. Page also lists many user-submitted grinder settings (e.g. Comandante 11-16, 1Zpresso JX 42-48 clicks, Baratza Encore 12-14), not part of the author's grind text.
segs: Pour 200 g, wetting all coffee; seat plunger ~1 cm to stop drips
Press gently all the way, ~30 s
why: A lean ratio and near-boiling water extract fully without stirring — a clear, tea-like cup that shows off delicate light roasts.

name: Lance Hedrick — A Very Good Recipe
author: Lance Hedrick
grind: Medium-fine (start coarser, French press / pour-over-like, and move finer until balanced)
notes: Standard-orientation bloom-and-swirl recipe aimed at cutting bitterness and astringency: slow gentle press, stop before the hiss, modest 92°C water. Dose scales with roast (15 g light, 16 g medium, 17 g dark) and temps drop for darker roasts (~88°C medium, 82–84°C dark).
issues: Bloom water amount not stated. Pour (bloom and main) durations, the 5 s swirls, and the 30 s press are estimated; page's 2:00 brew time is the steep before pressing. Page lists 250 g water but step says 'up to 250 mL'. Roast listed as light washed; 16 g/17 g given for medium/dark.
segs: Level bed, pour slowly a small bloom
Place plunger to stop drip, move off scale, swirl
Press gently, stop before the hiss; pull plunger up slightly
why: Built to cut bitterness and astringency with a gentle press — a safe, balanced recipe for medium beans with caramel and nut notes.

name: Lance Hedrick — Dark Roast & Decaf
author: Lance Hedrick
grind: Coarse, around 1200 micron (~800 burr movement); about 35 clicks on a Comandante or 65 clicks on a 1ZPRESSO ZP6
notes: Very high dose (1:4) concentrate at only 80°C with a coarse grind, then diluted; meant for decaf, dark, baked or aged coffee past its prime.
issues: Bypass is a range of 80–120 g; 100 g (midpoint) used. Bypass water temperature not stated (assumed hot). Pour and flip durations estimated; page lists 2:00 brew time but steps total ~2:10. Page title says 'Decaf and Dark Roast Version'; shared by Cpt Tziank.
why: Very cool water and a coarse grind on dark, decaf or aged coffee keep the chocolate and roast and drop the ashy bitterness.

name: Lance Hedrick — Light Roast Concentrate
author: Lance Hedrick
grind: Medium-coarse, around 1000 micron (650 or so burr movement)
